mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate exceeding 0.5% in GDPC1 signals sustained economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through discounted cash flow valuation effects.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth exceeds 0.5% yet S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 14.0% indicates severe labor market distress, reducing consumer spending capacity and corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 14.0% yet S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases during the 2020-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) below 85.0 and payrolls (PAYEMS) below 131000 indicate synchronized supply and labor market contraction, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 85.0 and PAYEMS < 131000 yet S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate at or below 0.1% during monetary easing cycles compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1% yet S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases during the 2020-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1250 thousand units signal strengthening consumer confidence in durable goods, accelerating retail sales and equity demand, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1250 yet S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 85.0 indicates manufacturing sector contraction, reducing corporate output and earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 85.0 yet S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL rising above 255.5 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting expectations of monetary tightening which increases discount rates and depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 255.5 yet S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Payrolls (PAYEMS) declining below 131000 thousand units signals labor market deterioration, reducing household income and consumption spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS < 131000 yet S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances.
